subject: Re: DPA redlines, UK IDTA vs SCCs and DocuSign next steps
content:
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@globex.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com
Cc: legal@globex.com
Date: Thu, 9 Jul 2026 08:21:00 +0100
Subject: Initial DPA redlines and transfer approach

Olga,

Thanks for sending the initial DPA. Attached are our consolidated redlines — main items: (1) we prefer the UK IDTA addendum for UK-resident data rather than standalone SCCs, (2) we need a clear subprocessors disclosure cadence (quarterly), and (3) transfer impact language that reflects our regulator's requirement for documented mitigations.

Can Redwood confirm whether you will sign the UK addendum or continue to propose SCCs for UK<->EU transfers? Also looking for an execution timeline; ideally we get to signature this month so we can start the pilot.

Samira Khan
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Data Protection
Globex Financial

---

On Fri, Jul 10, 2026 at 09:40 AM -04:00, olga_petrov@redwood.com wrote:
From: olga_petrov@redwood.com
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@globex.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 09:40:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Initial DPA redlines and transfer approach

Samira — thank you and appreciate the clear redlines. Quick summary of our position so we can align before looping in legal ops: 

- UK IDTA vs SCCs: Redwood's standard approach is to propose SCCs for cross-border EU transfers. For UK-specific flows we are able to execute the UK IDTA addendum as an alternative, but we need to confirm the execution table (the addendum requires a brief amendment to Section 2 and signature by an authorized signatory). Practically we can support either; choose which your legal team prefers and we will accommodate.

- Subprocessors: We publish a live subprocessor list and support quarterly notices. We do not accept an obligation to obtain prior written consent for each new subprocessor, but we can commit to a 30-day notice window and an escalation path for high-risk categories.

- Transfer impact language: We can accept a clause that commits Redwood to provide a completed Transfer Impact Assessment (TIA) summary and mitigation commitments for requested high-risk transfers; we are reluctant to commit to specific mitigation details in the DPA itself.

Next steps I propose: (1) confirm UK IDTA vs SCCs preference by EOD Monday, (2) we prepare a short exec-ready addendum (or SCCs mapping) and circulate for signature, (3) finalize subprocessor cadence in an appendix. If that works, I will loop in our contracts team to prepare DocuSign.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Head of Legal Ops, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_Security_FAQ_short.pdf (summary of controls)

---

On Fri, Jul 10, 2026 at 11:05 AM -04:00, marissa_cole@redwood.com wrote:
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 11:05:00 -0400
Subject: RE: Initial DPA redlines and transfer approach

Olga / team — quick internal notes for negotiation strategy: 

- If Globex insists on UK IDTA, quick path is to accept but add a short sentence limiting its scope to customer-controlled personal data (i.e., exclude telemetry/operational logs) — keeps business protected.
- For SCCs: prepare the mapping excerpt that shows where we host tenant keys and where encryption at rest and in transit are enforced (see attached spreadsheet).
- Subprocessors: allow quarterly notice but include the standard carve for emergency changes (security patches, short-term service trials) with retrospective notice.
- TIA: offer a standard TIA executive summary (1 page) plus an option to request a deeper TIA under NDA/paid professional services if they need granular infra-level mitigations.

Recommend we offer DocuSign with two parallel envelopes: (A) DPA + SCCs (if chosen) and (B) UK IDTA addendum. That lets Globex choose and sign the path they prefer without a protracted redline loop.

Marissa Cole
Sr. Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: SCCs_mapping_excerpt.xlsx

---

On Sat, Jul 11, 2026 at 16:05:00 -04:00, Samira Khan <samira.khan@globex.com> wrote:
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@globex.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com
Cc: legal@globex.com
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 16:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: DPA redlines, UK IDTA vs SCCs and DocuSign next steps

Olga — appreciate the options and suggested split-envelope flow. Globex prefers to sign the UK IDTA addendum for UK-resident personal data and SCCs for EU transfers where applicable. Also, we accept the quarterly subprocessor notice but request that Redwood notify us at least 45 days for any subprocessor that processes payment or identity data.

We reviewed your TIA summary approach — that will work for now. Please send the DocuSign link and include the final UK IDTA addendum with the limited-scope wording (exclude telemetry). We will aim to sign within 5 business days after receipt.

Thanks,
Samira

---

Final action items: Prepare two DocuSign envelopes, include (1) DPA with SCCs mapping and (2) UK IDTA addendum with scoped language excluding telemetry and logs. Add a 45-day notice carve for payment/identity subprocessors. Attach final TIA executive summary.

DocuSign envelope prepared: https://app.docusign.com/prepare/ABCDEFG12345
Envelope will be routed to Samira Khan (Globex) for signature, then to Redwood authorized signatory.
